over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

about how the deal was structured at closing.

# Outcome sub-dossier — frontdoor, inc. realized record, ~3-5-year horizon (fiscal year 2022)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The entity remained an independent SEC registrant
> filing its own annual reports; the outcome window is fixed at fiscal year 2022 (year
> ended December 31, 2022), reported in the Form 10-K filed March 1, 2023. This sub-dossier
> contains no information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status in the outcome window
- The entity remained an independent public registrant and filed an Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2022, from which the audited figures below are drawn. [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-23-000062, Form 10-K (FY2022), Item 7 / Item 8]

## Realized financial record (audited, FY2022 vs FY2021)
- Revenue was $1,662 million for the year ended December 31, 2022, up four percent from $1,602 million in 2021; renewal revenue rose to $1,203 million (from $1,103 million) while real-estate first-year revenue fell 27 percent to $184 million amid a challenging home-seller market. [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-23-000062, Form 10-K (FY2022), Item 7 Results of Operations]
- Net income was $71 million for 2022, down 45 percent from $128 million in 2021; income before income taxes fell to $93 million from $168 million. [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-23-000062, Form 10-K (FY2022), Item 7 Results of Operations]
- Restructuring charges were $20 million in 2022, up from $3 million in 2021. [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-23-000062, Form 10-K (FY2022), Item 7 Results of Operations]
- Total shareholders' equity was $61 million as of December 31, 2022, compared with $2 million as of December 31, 2021. [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-23-000062, Form 10-K (FY2022), Item 7 Financial Position]

## Documented product/process-interface disruption over time
- The entity had built a technology platform, Streem (augmented reality, computer vision and machine learning), which it was integrating into its core home-services business and also licensed to third-party business customers as software-as-a-service. [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-23-000062, Form 10-K (FY2022), Item 1 Business]
- During the third quarter of 2022 the entity identified indicators of potential impairment for the Streem reporting unit and performed an interim discounted-cash-flow analysis as of September 30, 2022, determining that the reporting unit's carrying amount exceeded its fair value. [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-23-000062, Form 10-K (FY2022), Critical Accounting Policies — Goodwill and Intangible Assets]
- A $14 million impairment charge was recognized in the third quarter of 2022, comprising the remaining net carrying amount of Streem's goodwill of $9 million and intangibles of $5 million. [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-23-000062, Form 10-K (FY2022), Item 7 / Notes]

## Documented operating trajectory and organizational change
- The number of home service plans declined to 2.13 million as of December 31, 2022 from 2.21 million a year earlier (a four percent reduction, versus a two percent reduction in 2021), while the customer retention rate rose to 75.7 percent from 74.2 percent. [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-23-000062, Form 10-K (FY2022), Item 7 Results of Operations]
- As of December 31, 2022 the entity had 1,712 employees (1,660 in the United States and 52 abroad, primarily in India providing technology services), none represented by a labor union, operating under a virtual-first work environment. [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-23-000062, Form 10-K (FY2022), Item 1 Human Capital Management]
- A leadership change occurred in the window: William C. Cobb entered an employment agreement with the entity dated May 19, 2022, and signed the FY2022 Form 10-K as Chairman of the Board, Director and Chief Executive Officer (principal executive officer). [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-23-000062, Form 10-K (FY2022), Exhibit Index item 10.21 and signature page]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Within the fixed FY2022 outcome window the entity remained an independent, going-concern public registrant with revenue up four percent to $1,662 million but net income down 45 percent to $71 million, elevated restructuring charges ($20 million), a modest decline in home-service-plan count (to 2.13 million) offset by improved retention (75.7 percent), a full $14 million impairment writing off the goodwill and intangibles of its Streem technology reporting unit whose acquired platform could not be aligned to support its carrying value, and a change of chief executive during 2022. [SRC: SEC accession 0001562762-23-000062, Form 10-K (FY2022), Items 1, 7 and 8 and signature page]

[SLICE END]
